sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Expansionist Doctrine**: Baji Rao I’s policy of 'striking at the trunk' of the Mughal tree rather than the branches, viewing Malwa as the gateway to Northern India.
• **Fiscal Mechanism**: The institutionalization of **Chauth** (1/4th of revenue for protection) and **Sardeshmukhi** (additional 1/10th for hereditary rights) as tools for resource extraction.
• **Strategic Geography**: Malwa served as a buffer zone and a vital transit route for trade and military movement between the Deccan and the Gangetic plains.
• **Key Metric**: The transition from 'Mulkgiri' (plunder-based raids) to 'Swarajya' (sovereign administration) marked the shift in Maratha governance.

items.definition: Military expeditions aimed at collecting tribute from territories without necessarily annexing them; the precursor to formal administration.
The architect of the 'Forward Policy' who transformed the Maratha state from a regional power into an all-India empire.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **The Forward Policy**: Shifting the focus from the Deccan to the Mughal heartland to weaken the central authority.
• **Alliance Building**: Strategic use of local chieftains and disgruntled Mughal nobles to facilitate Maratha entry.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Internal Factionalism**: Rivalries between Maratha chiefs (Gaekwad, Holkar, Scindia) often hindered unified administration.
• **Mughal Resistance**: Persistent, though weakening, attempts by the Nizam and Mughal governors to reclaim lost territories.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'G-M-A' (Gujarat, Malwa, Administration).
• **Decoded Meaning**: G (Gujarat - Wealth/Ports), M (Malwa - Gateway/Buffer), A (Administration - Chauth/Sardeshmukhi).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Chauth' collection with 'Land Revenue'. Chauth was a military tribute for protection, not a tax on land ownership.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Maratha Imperialism' to describe the shift from defensive guerrilla warfare to offensive territorial expansion.

keyTakeaways: The Maratha advance was not merely territorial but a systematic fiscal encroachment on Mughal resources.
Baji Rao I’s victory at Amjhera (1728) was the turning point for Maratha dominance in Central India.
The transition from Mulkgiri to formal administration created the 'Maratha Confederacy' structure.
